exact_statement: Determine whether the complete family of squarefree K_(d-1,d) prime-grid relations inside H_N forces an alteration-robust transversal lower bound of order N exp(-(2+o(1)) sqrt(log N log log N)), with an explicit finite-parameter inequality and optimized all-N asymptotic. Prove support minimality, distinctness, height and high-tail bounds, and quantify the consequence for uniform adaptive prime-valuation classifiers followed by arbitrary global repair. Do not claim an o(N) upper bound, an infinite density-one construction, a solution of Erdos 786, or Tier-1 novelty without an independent literature audit.
source: Derived from the audited K_(s+1,s) edge-prime circuit in erdos-786-distinct-factor-admission-20260824 and the global-alteration gap in erdos-786-square-root-query-barrier-20260827.
scope_notes: Variant lock: H_N has vertex set {2,...,N}; an edge is the support of two disjoint Finsets of distinct integers with equal products and unequal cardinalities.
For an integer d>=3, use d-1 disjoint prime pools, a (d-1)-by-d grid, row products of d primes, and column products of d-1 primes. Every selected cell prime occurs once on each shore.
The family contains all injective row choices from the frozen prime pools. A valid theorem must treat the whole overlapping family, not a single circuit or a disjoint packing.
The finite target is a lower bound for every transversal of the grid subhypergraph in terms of the common pool size m and d; the optimized target then follows by a proved prime-supply estimate.
The asymptotic target is for every sufficiently large integer N. Logs are natural. The dimension may depend on N and must be stated explicitly.
The high-tail statement must give an explicit lower threshold for every row and column product, not merely N^{1-o(1)} prose.
The alteration consequence permits an arbitrary second-stage deletion set chosen after the local classifier output; only its cardinality is charged.
A lower bound on tau(H_N) does not supply the required o(N) upper bound. The result cannot close either the finite or infinite form of Erdos 786.
The predecessor campaigns are read-only. Their audited single K_(s+1,s) circuit and square-root local-query theorem may be cited, but their claims may not be silently widened.

Ordinary prime-number-theorem input may be used for prime supply. Priority and journal-tier judgments remain pending until the scoped theorem has been independently reconstructed and literature checked.

frozen_finite_interface.prime_pools: pairwise disjoint P_1,...,P_r of common size m, all primes in (x/2,x]
frozen_finite_interface.target_inequality: every transversal D of the complete grid family satisfies d*|D_col|/m^(d-1)+|D_row|/binom(m,d)>=1, hence |D|>=min(m^(d-1)/d,binom(m,d))
frozen_finite_interface.matching_upper_comparator: deleting every possible column product gives a transversal of size m^(d-1)

frozen_asymptotic_interface.dimension_choice: d=floor(sqrt(log N/log log N)), adjusted to be at least 3
frozen_asymptotic_interface.pool_supply: partition primes in (x/2,x] equally among d-1 pools
frozen_asymptotic_interface.target: log tau(H_N)>=log N-(2+o(1))*sqrt(log N*log log N)
